headline: Exploited vCenter and Cisco Expressway flaws are due for patching by 23 November
plain_summary: Two flaws in widely used server software are being attacked and are on CISA's must-patch list with a 23 November deadline: VMware vCenter and Cisco Expressway. Google attributes the vCenter attacks to a suspected state-linked group. Separately, a supplier breach at PLAID has exposed customer data at many Japanese firms. Organisations running the affected products should patch now; others need no action beyond watching for phishing.

items.title: Google: vCenter zero-day CVE-2026-123890 used in espionage
items.why: Google says a suspected PRC-nexus group exploited this unauthenticated bypass from early September, and CISA lists it with a 23 November deadline.
items.action: Apply Broadcom's fixed vCenter builds (8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200 or 9.1.1.0200) now; vCenter 7.0 has no public patch. Restrict inbound access to and egress from vCenter, following the hardening advice in Google's post.

items.title: Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 exploited after public PoC
items.why: F6 reports an attack on clustered devices after a PoC was posted; Cisco's advisory still says it knows of no malicious use, and CISA's deadline is 23 November.
items.action: If you run clustered Expressway, upgrade to X15.5.20 now (X14 and earlier must move to a fixed release; Cisco says no workaround). If you cannot patch at once, F6 advises blocking TCP 4371-4372 except from trusted cluster node IPs.

items.title: NGINX HTTP/2 flaws allow remote code execution; PoC public
items.why: CERT-FR says two flaws allow unauthenticated code execution over HTTP/2 and a public proof of concept exists for one.
items.action: Check every NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus server that serves HTTP/2. Apply the fixed versions from F5 bulletins K000163926 and K000163928 (1.30.7 or 1.31.9), or disable HTTP/2 until patched. Review exposed servers for signs of compromise.

items.title: WordPress 7.1.5 fixes unauthenticated privilege escalation
items.why: The security release lists 20 items, including a flaw the project says could lead to remote code execution; no exploitation is reported.
items.action: Update WordPress to 7.1.5 now (Dashboard, Updates), or confirm the background auto-update ran; older branches are being backported, so watch for those releases.

items.title: ZOZO: about 15.18 million customers affected by PLAID KARTE leak
items.why: A breach at supplier PLAID's KARTE service has exposed customer data at ZOZO and other Japanese firms; card data is not confirmed leaked.
items.action: ZOZO customers: be wary of phishing emails, texts or calls impersonating ZOZO, and do not open their links or attachments, as ZOZO advises.

items.title: European Commission confirms AI-generated cyber campaign
items.why: The Commission says several applications were taken down, most are restored, and it has found no evidence of a staff-wide data breach.
items.action: If you work with EU institutions, expect notices from them and treat unexpected messages claiming to be from Commission staff with care.

items.title: Proximus mobile disruption: software bug, cyberattack ruled out
items.why: Proximus says a software update caused the disruption and rules out a cyberattack, per Belgian press reports.
